database_summary: This SQLite dataset models motor-racing (Formula 1 style) historical data. It contains descriptive tables for circuits, constructors, drivers and seasons; event/race metadata; per-race results, standings and session-level data (qualifying, sprint_results, lap_times, pit_stops); and a set of curated/extended tables (*_ext, short_*). Many tables are event/measured facts (lap_times, pit_stops, results) while others are descriptive/dimension-like (circuits, drivers, constructors). Several tables have composite natural keys (e.g. lap_times uses race_id, driver_id, lap). The dataset is suitable for queries about race results, lap/time analytics, standings and driver/constructor summaries. Joins between event tables and dimension tables are common; care is required where joins can multiply rows (for example joining results to lap_times or driver_standings to driver_standings_ext).

accepted.name: race_results_with_driver_constructor
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  results.result_id AS result_id,
  results.race_id AS race_id,
  results.driver_id AS driver_id,
  results.constructor_id AS constructor_id,
  results.number AS number,
  results.grid AS grid,
  results.position AS position,
  results.position_text AS position_text,
  results.position_order AS position_order,
  results.points AS points,
  results.laps AS laps,
  results.time AS time,
  results.milliseconds AS milliseconds,
  results.fastest_lap AS fastest_lap,
  results.rank AS rank,
  results.fastest_lap_time AS fastest_lap_time,
  results.fastest_lap_speed AS fastest_lap_speed,
  results.status_id AS status_id,
  drivers.driver_ref AS driver_ref,
  drivers.number AS driver_number,
  drivers.code AS code,
  drivers.forename AS forename,
  drivers.surname AS surname,
  drivers.dob AS dob,
  drivers.nationality AS nationality,
  constructors.constructor_ref AS constructor_ref,
  constructors.name AS constructor_name,
  constructors.nationality AS constructor_nationality,
  races.year AS year,
  races.round AS round,
  races.circuit_id AS circuit_id,
  races.name AS race_name,
  races.date AS race_date,
  races.time AS race_time
FROM results
LEFT JOIN drivers ON results.driver_id = drivers.driver_id
LEFT JOIN constructors ON results.constructor_id = constructors.constructor_id
LEFT JOIN races ON results.race_id = races.race_id
accepted.description: Denormalized per-race driver result rows augmented with driver and constructor attributes and race metadata. Useful when answering questions that join results to driver/constructor/race details (e.g., best finishes, points by driver in a race, grid vs finish comparisons). | Use for: List drivers and constructors for a given race with finishing positions and points; Compare grid position vs finishing position for drivers; Aggregate points by constructor/driver for a season or race subset

accepted.name: driver_lap_aggregates
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id AS race_id,
  driver_id AS driver_id,
  COUNT(lap) AS lap_count,
  MIN(milliseconds) AS best_lap_milliseconds,
  MAX(milliseconds) AS worst_lap_milliseconds,
  AVG(milliseconds) AS avg_lap_milliseconds
FROM lap_times
GROUP BY race_id, driver_id
accepted.description: Per-driver-per-race aggregated lap time measures derived from lap_times: min/avg/max milliseconds and lap counts. Use this for driver-level lap performance comparisons in a race or across races. | Use for: Which driver had the fastest single lap in a race; Compare average lap times between drivers in a race; Filter drivers by minimum lap count or average lap performance

accepted.name: best_qualifying_per_driver_race
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  qualify_id AS qualify_id,
  race_id AS race_id,
  driver_id AS driver_id,
  constructor_id AS constructor_id,
  number AS number,
  position AS position,
  q1 AS q1,
  q2 AS q2,
  q3 AS q3,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY race_id ORDER BY position) AS qual_rank,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY race_id, driver_id ORDER BY COALESCE(position, 9999)) AS driver_best_attempt_rank
FROM qualifying
accepted.description: Ranks qualifying positions per race and driver; exposes qualify position and a rank so downstream queries can implement Top-K or pick the best qualifying attempt. Useful for top qualifiers, pole position detection, and per-driver best-qualifying selection when multiple records exist. | Use for: Find the pole sitter (qual_rank = 1) for each race; Select each driver's best qualifying record per race; List top-N qualifiers for a race using qual_rank <= N

accepted.name: race_fastest_lap_per_driver
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id AS race_id,
  driver_id AS driver_id,
  MIN(fastest_lap) AS fastest_lap_number,
  MIN(fastest_lap_time) AS fastest_lap_time
FROM results
WHERE fastest_lap IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY race_id, driver_id
accepted.description: Per-race per-driver fastest lap extracted from results' fastest_lap and fastest_lap_time / fastest_lap_speed fields. Useful for analyses that compare fastest laps across drivers or identify who set the fastest lap in a race. | Use for: Who achieved the fastest lap for each driver in a race; Determine the single fastest lap across all drivers in a race

accepted.name: pit_stop_aggregates_per_driver_race
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id AS race_id,
  driver_id AS driver_id,
  COUNT(stop) AS pit_stop_count,
  AVG(milliseconds) AS avg_pit_milliseconds
FROM pit_stops
GROUP BY race_id, driver_id
accepted.description: Per-driver-per-race aggregated pit stop metrics: total pit stop count and average/median milliseconds (median approximated by simple AVG since SQLite has no median). Useful for pit strategy and reliability analyses. | Use for: Which drivers took the most pit stops in a race; Average pit stop duration by driver/race

accepted.name: driver_season_points
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  races.year AS year,
  results.driver_id AS driver_id,
  SUM(results.points) AS season_points,
  COUNT(DISTINCT results.race_id) AS races_contested
FROM results
JOIN races ON results.race_id = races.race_id
GROUP BY races.year, results.driver_id
accepted.description: Total points per driver per season-year by aggregating results joined to races to get the year. Useful for season standings, ranking drivers by points, or trend analysis across seasons. | Use for: Rank drivers by points in a season; Compute points per race or races contested per driver in a season

accepted.name: latest_race_per_year
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id AS race_id,
  year AS year,
  round AS round,
  date AS date,
  time AS time,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY date DESC, time DESC) AS race_in_year_rank
FROM races
accepted.description: Identifies the latest race (by date/time) for each year. Exposes a year-level ranking so downstream queries can pick the last race of a season. Useful for analyses anchored at season finale. | Use for: Select season finale race_id per year (race_in_year_rank = 1); Compare statistics at the end of season across years

accepted.name: driver_full_name_lookup
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  driver_id AS driver_id,
  driver_ref AS driver_ref,
  number AS number,
  code AS code,
  forename AS forename,
  surname AS surname,
  (COALESCE(forename, '') || ' ' || COALESCE(surname, '')) AS full_name,
  dob AS dob,
  nationality AS nationality,
  url AS url
FROM drivers
accepted.description: Normalized driver identity with a computed full_name column (forename + ' ' + surname) to simplify display and matching. Preserves original driver_id and other attributes for joins. | Use for: Display driver full names alongside results or standings; Match on driver names or present formatted driver labels
